questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Castles in the air
questions.solution:
The correct answer is:** Unrealistic and impossible plan**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The idiom **"Castles in the air"** refers to plans, hopes, or dreams that are unrealistic and unlikely to happen. (हवाई किले)

 
 
• **Example:** She keeps talking about moving to Hollywood and becoming a movie star, but those are just castles in the air.
 
 
 
• **"Unrealistic and impossible plan"** means a plan or idea that is not practical or feasible in reality. (अवास्तविक और असंभव योजना)
 
 
• **Example:** His dream of building a spaceship in his backyard is an unrealistic and impossible plan.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Unrealistic and impossible plan.**

questions.question:

questions.solution:

__
 
• The word **"acumulation"** is incorrectly spelled. It should be **"accumulation"**.
 
• **Meaning:** The process of gradually increasing or gathering together. (संचय)
 
 
• **Example:** The accumulation of snow on the roads made driving hazardous.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Environmental **(पर्यावरणीय): Relating to the natural world and the impact of human activity on its condition.

 
 
• **Example:** Environmental conservation efforts are crucial for maintaining biodiversity.
 
 
 
• **Atmosphere **(वायुमंडल): The envelope of gases surrounding the earth or another planet.
 
 
• **Example:** The Earth's atmosphere is essential for sustaining life.
 
 
 
• **Decades** (दशक): Periods of ten years.
 
 
• **Example:** Over the past few decades, technology has advanced at an unprecedented rate.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The manager asked me __if I have completed my projects__.

options.text: if he has completed my projects
if I has completed my projects
if I had completed my projects
if I shall have completed my projects

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. this part of the sentence has an error.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the second part of the given sentence, the singular form of the verb 'have' is incorrect.
 
• The verb form **"had"** is used because the sentence is in the **past perfect tense**.
 
• The manager's question about the completion of projects refers to an action that was completed before another action in the past (the moment the manager asked).
 
• Hence, **"had completed"** correctly indicates that the projects were finished prior to being asked.
 
• Therefore, the past perfect form of the verb 'had' should be used in place of the present perfect form 'have'.

Correct sentence: *The manager asked me if I **had completed** my projects*.

• The word **"Pause indecisively"** means to stop temporarily because of uncertainty or doubt. (अनिर्णय की स्थिति में रुकना)

• **"Hesitate"** refers to pausing before saying or doing something, often due to uncertainty or nervousness. (हिचकिचाना)

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error and select the option which rectifies that error.

The SNAP - 10 A / was launched on 3 April 1965 / on a Atlas - Agena D rocket / from Vandenberg Air Force Base.

options.text: on an Atlas - Agena D rocket

questions.solution:
The corrected form of the erroneous part is: on an **Atlas - Agena D rocket.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the third part of the given sentence, the article 'a' is incorrect.
 
• The correct article to use before a word starting with a vowel sound is 'an'.
 
• Therefore, the correct form should be 'on an Atlas - Agena D rocket'.

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Correct sentence: *The SNAP - 10 A was launched on 3 April 1965 on **an **Atlas - Agena D rocket from Vandenberg Air Force Base*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When choosing between 'a' and 'an', use 'a' before words that start with a consonant sound, and 'an' before words that start with a vowel sound.
 
 
• **Example:** *An apple a day keeps the doctor away.*
 
 
 
• Some words that start with a consonant letter might have a vowel sound, and vice versa, so it's important to focus on the sound rather than the letter.
 
 
• Example: *An hour, a university.*

questions.question:
Parts of the given sentence have been underlined. One of them contains an error. The underlined parts are given as options with some changes. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error.

This car is __lesser__ expensive than the __one__ I had __come to__ buy.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **less**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the word 'lesser' is incorrect.
 
• The correct comparative form of **'less'** is **'less'** itself, not 'lesser'.
 
• Therefore, the correct form should be 'less' instead of 'lesser'.

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Correct sentence: *This car is less expensive than the one I had come to buy*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The word **'less'** is used to describe a smaller amount of something that cannot be counted (uncountable nouns), whereas **'lesser'** is used in certain fixed expressions or to emphasize something's importance or quality.

 
 
• **Example:** *He was no lesser a man than his father*.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into four parts. Identify the part that contains an error.

(A) It is said / (B) that fortune / (C) favour the / (D) brave.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'C' i.e. this part of the sentence has an error.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the third part of the given sentence, the plural form of the verb 'favour' is incorrect.
 
• In the given sentence, the subject **'fortune'** is **singular**.
 
• If the **subject** is **singular**, the **verb **must also be **singular **to maintain **subject-verb agreement**.
 
 
• **Example:** *He **favours** the brave.*
 
 
 
• Therefore, the singular form of the verb 'favours' should be used in place of the plural form 'favour'.

Correct sentence: *It is said that fortune **favours** the brave*.

questions.question:

Teenage is that phase of life when __you are proposed to__ the world outside.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'you are exposed to'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the given sentence, the phrase 'you are proposed to' is incorrect and should be replaced.
 
• The correct phrase should be 'you are exposed to' as it makes the sentence grammatically correct and meaningful.
 
• The phrase "you are exposed to" is contextually correct in the sentence because it accurately describes the experience of teenagers encountering new experiences, ideas, and environments beyond their familiar surroundings.
 
• The passive construction "are exposed to" emphasizes the impact of the external world on teenagers during this phase of life, highlighting the influence and newness of these encounters.
 
• The sentence should read: ***Teenage is that phase of life when you are exposed to the world outside.***

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.
